card.statement:
1.

To define the category $\mathrm{P}_{G_{X,\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X},\mathbf{k})$ we use a slight variant of the constructions of Appendix A, where algebraic groups are replaced by group schemes over $X$ . This does not require any new ingredient: one simply replaces products by fiber products over $X$ everywhere.
The same remarks as in §A.4 are also in order here: we must consider perverse sheaves supported on a closed finite union of $G_{X,\mathcal{O}}$ -orbits, and equivariant under some quotient $(G/H_{n})_{X,\mathcal{O}}$ . (A more sensible definition of a category of perverse sheaves on $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ is due to Reich; see [Z4, §5.4]. These more sophisticated considerations will not be needed here.)

2.

It will follows from Lemma 7.10 below that in fact $\mathscr{M}\star_{X}\mathscr{N}$ is a perverse sheaf. This perverse sheaf is clearly $G_{X,\mathcal{O}}$ -equivariant, so that this operation indeed defines a functor from $\mathrm{P}_{G_{X,\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X},\mathbf{k})\times\mathrm{P}_{G_{X,\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X},\mathbf{k})$ to $\mathrm{P}_{G_{X,\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X},\mathbf{k})$ .

For the sake of simplicity,2222
22

The general situation can be
dealt with by putting the torsor of change of coordinates into the picture; see e.g. [Ga, §2.1.2] or [Z4, Discussion surrounding (3.1.10)] for details. from now on we restrict to the special case $X=\mathbb{A}^{1}$ . We can then
use a global coordinate on $X$ , which yields a local coordinate at any
point $x\in X$ , and therefore allows to identify $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,x}$ with the
affine Grassmannian $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ as we originally defined it. This also leads to
an identification $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}=\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}\times X$ . We let $\tau:\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\to\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ be
the projection and define $\tau^{\circ}:=\tau^{*}[1]\cong\tau^{!}[-1]$ ; the shift is introduced
so that $\tau^{\circ}$ takes a perverse sheaf on $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ to a perverse sheaf
on $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ .

We explained in §7.3 that the restriction of $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$ to the diagonal
$\Delta_{X}$ in $X^{2}$ is isomorphic to $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ ; we may then denote by
$i:\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}=\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}\bigl|_{\Delta_{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$
the closed embedding, and consider the functors $i^{\circ}:=i^{*}[-1]$ and $i^{\bullet}:=i^{!}[1]$ .
card.label: Remark 7.7

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
